title: Work IQ: long-running tasks for A2A and MCP agents
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing and documented controls are supported. The spending-policy API note should name the request-body properties that set the limits and selected services; documentation still leaves the long-running task lifecycle and feature-specific controls open.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans durable long-running Work IQ tasks.
claims.quote: Enable durable long-running A2A and MCP tasks with progress tracking, later result retrieval, and cancellation.

claims.claim: The planned tasks support both A2A and MCP.
claims.quote: Enable durable long-running A2A and MCP tasks

claims.claim: The planned tasks provide progress tracking.
claims.quote: with progress tracking

claims.claim: The planned tasks support later result retrieval.
claims.quote: later result retrieval

claims.claim: Cancellation is part of the planned capability.
claims.quote: later result retrieval, and cancellation.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Work IQ API uses a consumption licensing model.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a consumption-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.claim: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ in custom and third-party agents is subject to usage-based billing.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents. It is subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.

claims.claim: Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license are billed based on usage.
claims.quote: Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license are billed based on usage.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API shares the credit pool with eligible services including Copilot Cowork and Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork, Copilot Studio agents, and Work IQ API can consume Copilot credits from a shared tenant pool.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Pricing, credit rates and limits specific to long-running tasks are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ long-running tasks Copilot Credits pricing rates limits spending policy resume; "Work IQ" "long-running" "pricing". Read Work IQ overview, Plan licensing and cost, billing management and monitoring; results describe general Work IQ charges, not a long-running-task rate or limit.

claims.claim: Work IQ work can fail with QuotaExhausted even when the tenant has prepaid credits.
claims.quote: A Work IQ chat request can fail with `QuotaExhausted` and the message "No AI credits are currently available for this user. Please request more credits from your admin." This error can happen even when the tenant has prepaid credits.

claims.claim: A Microsoft 365 Copilot license does not replenish the Work IQ API credit balance.
claims.quote: A Microsoft 365 Copilot license doesn't replenish the Work IQ API credit balance.

claims.claim: Spending policies set spending limits but do not reserve or allocate credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies control access and spending limits; they don't reserve or allocate credits for a workload, user, or group.

claims.claim: A spending policy can exclude Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Include Cowork and exclude Work IQ API from a policy when its users shouldn't consume credits through Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Excluding Work IQ API from one policy does not exclude it from other policies.
claims.quote: Review all applicable policies, including the default policy. Excluding a service from one policy doesn't exclude it from other policies.

claims.claim: A running task for a user in a group spending policy can finish without interruption after exceeding the per-user limit.
claims.quote: Users in a group spending policy that exceed their per-user spending limit: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.claim: That excess usage does not count toward the policy limit.
claims.quote: The excess usage doesn't count toward the policy limit, isn't billed (at Microsoft's sole discretion), and doesn't appear as consumed credits in the Cost Management dashboards

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP request policy is reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: No automation call for the Work IQ MCP request policy is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy settings API update policy tenant Graph PowerShell Allowed Disallowed; "Work IQ" "policy" "PATCH". Read policy governance and MCP overview; search returned generic configuration advice and unrelated Graph policies, not a Work IQ policy-setting endpoint.

claims.claim: Initial Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-level on/off.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.claim: Per-user, per-app and per-agent policy controls are not in the initial Work IQ MCP policy control surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply across the tenant.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP mutation operations are not allowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety.

claims.claim: The mutation restriction includes create, update, delete and sending email.
claims.quote: This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported MCP mutation scenarios through tenant policy.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.claim: The Work IQ in Copilot Studio page says write operations are on by default for that experience.
claims.quote: Write operations are on by default. Your organization's permissions and policies still apply.

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio write-operation default remains subject to organization permissions and policies.
claims.quote: Write operations are on by default, subject to those permissions and policies.

claims.claim: The cited MCP policy is documented for MCP requests, not specifically for long-running task processing.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ A2A MCP long-running tasks default enabled tenant switch administrator cancellation progress reporting retention results storage; Work IQ long-running tasks Copilot Credits pricing rates limits spending policy resume. Read MCP policy governance: request-time control, no task lifecycle.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not specify whether MCP policy is re-evaluated when a long-running task resumes.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ long-running A2A task delegated authentication token lifetime audit events cancellation user permissions resume; "Work IQ" "policy" "PATCH". Read Work IQ overview, MCP policy governance and A2A overview: per-request enforcement is stated, but task-resumption behavior is not.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Spending policy creation is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates a spending policy specifying credit limits and selected services.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies
Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.
claims.fix: Append to controls[1].note and its rendered table note: "The request body sets periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings." These properties are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/spendingpolicy-create.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy requires CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Creating a policy without an initial audience (assignedGroups omitted or empty) requires only CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All.

claims.claim: A nonempty assignedGroups collection at creation additionally requires CopilotCostManagement-Assignment.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Supplying a nonempty assignedGroups collection at creation additionally requires CopilotCostManagement-Assignment.ReadWrite.All.

claims.claim: Spending policy creation also requires Billing Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: At runtime, creating a policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.

claims.claim: The API creates a spending policy disabled.
claims.quote: A new policy is created disabled.

claims.claim: The documented group-policy safe-create sequence links the audience through Add assigned group.
claims.quote: For a group-scoped policy, follow the safe-create sequence: create the policy disabled, link its audience with Add assigned group, and let the service enable it once its requirements are satisfied.

claims.claim: Spending-policy creation requires @odata.type, displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings.
claims.quote: In the request body, supply a JSON representation of a spendingPolicy object with a concrete @odata.type. Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.

claims.claim: The Cost Management APIs are beta, subject to change and not supported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The service usage API reports exactly one completed UTC day per call.
